items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: I took Johnny with me when Johnny couldn't play home street

ctx.x: Where was it? Oh, yeah, yeah. St. Charles. St. Charles. You know, I played one of my early things there. I played on Charlotte Street. You remember that? Yeah, but that was that. That's where the Yeah, but that was that. That's where the Yeah, but that was that. That's where the You know where the Regents used to be? Central Rattestate.

Yeah. We used to have a The Regents used to be? Yeah. We went to Canal and Burgundy and they made us get off Canal Street, Tordish had. Then we moved up. Man, there was nothing but- Why did they make you get off Canal Street? Too much rascality around there, you know what I mean? Then we went on St. Charles Street. You know what Johnny biased off? Johnny started off there too. Johnny and I. Johnny and I. Johnny played with you. I took Johnny with me when Johnny couldn't play home street, home without home street.…

I ain't seen Johnny in 30s. He was driving a cab the last time I saw him. Oh, no. I ain't seen him in 30s in Rochester. Yeah? I had all. I broke them up. I broke for Thoreau and all of them. Johnny biased off? Yeah. I didn't know that. I always thought you worked for the government. You might. I don't know. I got into a veteran's care.
